scope: Claims supported by the shipped aggregate panels and result files.

allowed.claim: The simulated last-in-queue touch quoter has negative 10-second pre-fee entry markout on Bybit, Binance and Hyperliquid.
allowed.qualification: This is a one-sided entry markout, not realised maker profit or loss.

allowed.claim: The two-way month-and-coin intervals for the pooled 10-second entry markout exclude zero on all three venues.
allowed.qualification: The panels cover different calendars and coin sets.

allowed.claim: The same-date Bybit-minus-Hyperliquid estimate is negative in the shipped re-quote panel.
allowed.qualification: The estimate depends on the extraction and re-quote specification and is not a causal architecture comparison.

allowed.claim: The matched lead-lag panel has a median 500 ms Bybit lead.
allowed.qualification: The 441 ms publication-cadence gap is of the same order, so the result does not establish an information lead.

allowed.claim: No session block shows a detectable calm-to-stress change in net entry markout under the specified sign test.
allowed.qualification: The test is Bybit-only and low powered; failure to reject is not invariance.

allowed.claim: In the 300-coin-day Bybit bid-side depth panel, the minimum measured break-even rebate is 0.328 bp and the touch overtakes the deepest level at 0.771 bp.
allowed.qualification: Levels are price depth, not queue position, and the published 1.5 bp tier is not shown to be attainable by this quoter.

allowed.claim: The tested Avellaneda-Stoikov depth rule remains negative on 66 of 91 coin-days and takes about 9.2 percent as many fills as the touch rule.
allowed.qualification: This is one limited quoting arm, not a general test of inventory-aware market making.

allowed.claim: All eight shipped aggregate panels rebuild byte-for-byte from the frozen derived measurement artifacts named in the lineage manifest.
allowed.qualification: Raw venue archives and the raw-to-derived measurement stage are outside this repository.

prohibited: Market makers lose money on these venues.
The study measures realised maker profitability.
Venue architecture causes the observed difference.
Bybit has an information lead over Hyperliquid.
Deeper queue position improves the result.
The adverse-to-capture ratio of 1.8 to 5.1 is a robust headline effect.
The simulated quoter qualifies for the published 1.5 bp rebate tier.
Net entry markout is unchanged or invariant across volatility regimes.
This repository reproduces the study from raw venue archives.
The result is a tradeable edge or a walk-forward strategy result.
